notes.b: The Food Studies practical coursework is worth 20% of the total marks in Home Economics Scientific and Social for every candidate, with the written paper carrying the rest. Each assignment is recorded in the SEC's digital Food Studies Practical Coursework Journal, so you need to know how the marks are split.
points: Each assignment is recorded under four headings: Investigation, Planning and Preparation, Implementation and Evaluation.
Investigation (the analysis and research) is marked out of 32, the largest share, so it is the part to give most time to.
Planning and Preparation is marked out of 8, for the ingredients with quantities and costing and for the key equipment.
Implementation is marked out of 28, for the procedure followed, the key factors considered, and safety and hygiene.
Evaluation is marked out of 12, for the implementation and for the specific requirements of the assignment.
The four headings total 80 marks for each assignment (32 + 8 + 28 + 12).
For 2027 candidates present two of the five assignments the SEC set, and where more than two are presented the two highest-scoring assignments count. The completion date was 2 November 2026.
The assignment brief still prints the standing instruction to complete four assignments, but the SEC's Assessment Arrangements 2027 override it, so the 2027 number is two of five.
notes.tip: Learn the 32, 8, 28 and 12 split and that it totals 80. Write two of five for 2027, not four, and say that the brief's standing wording is overridden.

notes.b: Every assignment falls under one of five areas of practice, and the investigation for that assignment covers the points set for its area.
points: Area A: Application of Nutritional Principles, such as planning meals for a particular nutritional need.
Area B: Food Preparation and Cooking Processes, involving new skills or equipment, so you learn and use something new.
Area C: Food Technology.
Area D: Properties of a Food, such as the effect of a marinade.
Area E: Comparative Analysis, including Sensory Analysis.
No Area C assignment was set for 2027, so the five assignments are spread across the other four areas.
notes.tip: Be ready to say which area an assignment falls in, for example that a marinade assignment is Area D and a granola comparison is Area E.

notes.b: The investigation is the biggest part of the marks, and what it must contain depends on the area. In every area, sources of information are cited.
points: Area A: the nutritional needs being investigated, the appropriate meal-planning guidelines, and suitable or modified dishes, meaning dishes that suit those needs or are adapted to meet them.
Area B: the preparation process, skill or equipment, the key points for success, and dishes that illustrate it, so the research shows why the technique works.
Area C: the processing method and its principles, containers, packaging and labelling, and suitable foods or dishes, for example the container that suits the method.
Area D: the definition of the property, the principles associated with it, and dishes that illustrate it, because the dishes show the property at work.
Area E: the testing technique and its possible outcomes, the foods or products tested, and the conditions that must be controlled so that the test is fair.
notes.tip: Examiners expect you to know what the investigation for a given area must include. Match the area to its list: needs and guidelines for A, process and key points for B, property and principles for D, test and controlled conditions for E.

notes.h: Rules for dishes, sources and group work
notes.b: The coursework has rules about what you cook, how you work and how you present your written record.
points: Dishes must meet the requirements of the assignment, so that the dish can earn the marks for it.
A dish may not be repeated, or partially repeated, across assignments, so each assignment needs its own dish.
Fresh foods should be used rather than convenience foods (ready-made or pre-prepared products), so that the cooking is your own work.
Practical work may be done in pairs, or in groups for Area E only.
The written record must be the candidate's own work, even where the practical work was shared.
Every area requires sources of information to be cited, and all sources must be referenced, including AI-generated material.
notes.tip: The rules to remember are no repeated dishes, fresh foods, your own written record, and all sources referenced, AI included.

notes.h: The 2027 assignments: Areas A and B
notes.b: The SEC set five assignments for 2027. Each links to theory you study elsewhere in the course, named here by subject.
points: Assignment 1 (Area A): the challenges older people face in keeping a healthy diet; their nutritional needs and meal-planning guidelines; two-course main-meal menus; preparation of one main course. The theory is meal planning for older people and special diets.

Assignment 2 (Area A): the causes and effects of iron deficiency; the nutritional needs and meal-planning factors for reducing the risk; two-course main-meal menus; preparation of one main course. The theory is minerals (iron) and meal planning.
Assignment 3 (Area B): commercially prepared filo and puff pastry, covering brands, forms, ingredients, cost, and sweet and savoury dishes.

Assignment 3 also asks for the key points for success with one of the pastries, preparation of one dish, and evaluation of the advantages and disadvantages of the chosen pastry. The theory is pastry, taught with cereals and grains, and it is the background knowledge the practical rests on.
notes.tip: The written paper does not examine the coursework itself, but it does examine its themes: older people's meal planning, iron deficiency and pastry. Revise the theory behind each assignment.

notes.h: The 2027 assignments: Areas D and E
notes.b: The remaining two assignments cover the property of a food and a comparison of products by sensory testing.
points: No Area C assignment was set for 2027.

Assignment 4 (Area D): types of marinade and the dishes that use each; the benefits of marinating and its underlying principles; the key points for success; preparation of one marinated dish; evaluation of whether the marinade achieved its purpose. The theory is meat tenderising.
Assignment 5 (Area E): descriptive rating tests and their use in the food industry; the range of commercial granola, covering brands, ingredients, nutritional content and cost.

Assignment 5 also asks for a descriptive rating test on two similar brands using six agreed sensory attributes and star diagrams, then a comparison of the two sensory profiles. The theory is sensory analysis, taught with food additives and processing.
notes.tip: Marinades and tenderising, and sensory analysis, are themes the written paper can examine. Know the theory behind Assignments 4 and 5 as well as the practical.

keyTerms.definition: The analysis and research section of each coursework assignment, which cites all sources of information.
Testing food with the senses to describe its characteristics and to compare products.
A sensory test in which a panel rates agreed attributes of a product on a scale.
A radial chart in which each arm shows the rated strength of one sensory attribute, so that two products can be compared at a glance.
A seasoned liquid in which food is soaked before cooking to add flavour and tenderise it.
Very thin, stretched sheets of dough that are brushed with fat between layers and baked to a crisp finish.
A laminated pastry made from layers of dough and fat, rolled and folded so that it rises in the oven.
The comparison of two or more similar products by testing to identify their differences.
A prepared food that reduces preparation and cooking time, which coursework dishes should avoid in favour of fresh foods.

questions.prompt: Outline the four headings under which each Food Studies coursework assignment is marked, giving the marks for each.
questions.model: Investigation (analysis and research): 32 marks. Planning and Preparation (ingredients with quantities and costing, and key equipment): 8 marks. Implementation (the procedure followed, the key factors considered, and safety and hygiene): 28 marks. Evaluation (of the implementation and of the specific requirements of the assignment): 12 marks. Total for each assignment: 80 marks.

questions.prompt: Discuss what must be covered in an Area E coursework investigation, including the sensory test, the foods tested and the conditions that must be controlled.
questions.model: Area E is Comparative Analysis, including Sensory Analysis. The investigation must describe the testing technique and its possible outcomes. A descriptive rating test uses a panel that rates agreed sensory attributes, such as appearance, aroma, flavour, texture and aftertaste, for each product. The results can be shown on star diagrams so that the two sensory profiles can be compared. The foods or products tested, such as two similar brands of a product, must be identified with their ingredients, nutritional content and cost. The conditions to control include the place and timing of the test, the number and type of tasters, hygiene and equipment, the temperature at which the samples are served, the sample quantity and uniformity, the coding of samples and the order in which they are presented. Sources of information must be cited, and the written record must be the candidate's own work even where the practical work was done in a group.
